description: Urban FIA is the US Forest Service's inventory of trees and forests in urban areas, extending the national forest inventory to cities to track the status and trends of urban trees, the services they provide, their health and their future risk from insects and disease. It covers, at full implementation, all urban areas across all states with added focus on more than 100 cities; participating cities have about 200 randomly selected field plots, each a circular plot of 48 ft radius where crews record tree species, heights, diameters, health, other vegetation, ground cover and land use, remeasured typically every 5 to 7 years. It is run by the Forest Inventory and Analysis program of the USDA Forest Service with methods fused with the i-Tree software suite, and it has three components: data collection, the Urban National Landowner Survey (on hiatus) and Urban Wood Flows. Data are available through the Urban DataMart, which offers downloadable data, the My City's Trees application and published papers; the programme page describes public availability but does not state a licence. Caveats: the landowner survey is paused, and the other two components are more limited in scope than plot collection. It supports urban green infrastructure baselines, tree risk and storm damage exposure analysis, and ecosystem service modelling for climate adaptation; a related record is the i-Tree model suite.
